query: .schema (read-only dump of table definitions)
result: Eight tables: badges, comments, postHistory, postLinks, posts, tags, users, votes. Column names as used throughout this version were read directly from these definitions.
validation_method: read-only schema inspection

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM each of badges, comments, postHistory, postLinks, posts, tags, users, votes
result: badges 79851; comments 174285; postHistory 303155; postLinks 11102; posts 91966; tags 1032; users 40325; votes 38930.
validation_method: independent row count per table

query: PRAGMA table_info for each table, filtered to date-like column names
result: posts exposes the creation timestamp under a misspelled name (the letters of the word being transposed) and its activity timestamp under a similarly misspelled name. badges uses Date; comments, postHistory, postLinks, users and votes use the conventional CreationDate spelling. The posts table has no conventionally spelled creation column.
validation_method: column-name inspection across all tables

query: SELECT min/max of users.CreationDate, users.LastAccessDate, posts.CreaionDate, and sample values from badges.Date and votes.CreationDate
result: users range 2010-07-19 06:55:26.0 to 2014-09-14 01:01:44.0; posts range 2009-02-02 14:21:12.0 to 2014-09-14 02:09:23.0; badges values carry a trailing fractional component; votes.CreationDate values are day-precision such as 2010-07-19. Formatting therefore varies by table.
validation_method: boundary and sample value inspection

query: SELECT min/max CreationDate and LastAccessDate FROM users
result: Account creation spans 2010-07-19 to 2014-09-14; last access spans 2010-07-19 to 2014-09-14 03:05:57. Post content begins earlier than the earliest account, at 2009-02-02.
validation_method: boundary inspection

query: SELECT PostTypeId, COUNT(*) FROM posts GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
result: 1=42912, 2=47755, 3=6, 4=639, 5=640, 6=9, 7=5. The two dominant codes are questions and answers; the remaining codes form a small tail of wiki and nomination posts.
validation_method: enumeration distribution

query: SELECT Id, PostTypeId, Title, length(Body) FROM posts WHERE PostTypeId IN (3,4,5,6,7) ORDER BY PostTypeId LIMIT 8
result: Rows of these codes carry body content but no title and no tags; the excerpt and wiki codes appear in adjacent identifier pairs.
validation_method: sample row inspection

query: SELECT Id, TagName, Count, ExcerptPostId, WikiPostId FROM tags LIMIT 5; SELECT Tags FROM posts WHERE Id=1
result: tags.TagName holds bare lower-case names such as 'bayesian', 'prior', 'elicitation', 'normality', 'open-source'. The tag list on a question is a concatenation of bracketed tokens with no separator, for example '<bayesian><prior><elicitation>'.
validation_method: side-by-side value comparison of both representations

query: SELECT * FROM tags WHERE TagName LIKE '%bayesian%'
result: Four tags match the substring: 'bayesian' (1342 questions), 'hierarchical-bayesian' (103), 'bayesian-network' (26), 'bayesian-score' (3). A bare substring search therefore conflates four distinct topics, while the bracketed token form distinguishes them.
validation_method: substring match demonstrating over-collection

query: SELECT PostTypeId, COUNT(Tags) FROM posts GROUP BY 1
result: Tag lists are populated for 42912 rows, all of PostTypeId 1, and for zero rows of every other post kind. This exactly equals the question count.
validation_method: non-null count grouped by post type

query: SELECT t.TagName, t.ExcerptPostId, t.WikiPostId, p.PostTypeId FROM tags t LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.Id=t.ExcerptPostId WHERE t.TagName LIKE '%bayesian%'
result: For TagName 'bayesian', ExcerptPostId is 20258 and WikiPostId is 20257; post 20258 carries the excerpt post type and post 20257 the full wiki post type. The compound bayesian tags have neither reference.
validation_method: reference resolution against the posts table

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts; SELECT COUNT(ViewCount) FROM posts; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts WHERE PostTypeId=1
result: ViewCount is non-null for 42912 rows of 91966, exactly the question count; it is absent for every answer and wiki post.
validation_method: non-null count compared against post-type counts

query: SELECT COUNT(FavoriteCount) FROM posts
result: 13243 non-null values against 42912 question posts, so roughly two thirds of questions carry no favourite value.
validation_method: non-null count compared against question count

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts WHERE FavoriteCount IS NOT NULL
result: The favourite counter is the only measure in the dataset that reflects users bookmarking content; it is independent of the score and view counters on the same row.
validation_method: column semantics inspection

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts; SELECT COUNT(ParentId) FROM posts; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts WHERE PostTypeId=2
result: ParentId is non-null for 47755 rows, exactly the answer count, confirming that the parent reference identifies the question an answer responds to.
validation_method: non-null count compared against answer count

query: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN p.AnswerCount <> COALESCE(a.n,0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM posts p LEFT JOIN (SELECT ParentId, COUNT(*) n FROM posts WHERE PostTypeId=2 GROUP BY ParentId) a ON a.ParentId=p.Id
result: Zero mismatches: the denormalised answer counter agrees with the actual answer rows for every post.
validation_method: reconciliation of counter against underlying rows

query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS posts_checked, SUM(CASE WHEN p.CommentCount <> COALESCE(c.n,0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS mismatched FROM posts p LEFT JOIN (SELECT PostId, COUNT(*) n FROM comments GROUP BY PostId) c ON c.PostId=p.Id
result: 91966 posts checked, 20 mismatched. The denormalised comment counter agrees with the underlying comment rows for all but 20 posts, so a counter of zero reliably expresses 'no comments'.
validation_method: reconciliation of counter against underlying rows

query: SELECT (UserId IS NULL), (UserDisplayName IS NULL), COUNT(*) FROM comments GROUP BY 1,2
result: 171450 rows have the account reference present and the embedded label null; 2831 rows have the account reference null and the embedded label present; 4 rows have neither. The two fields are effectively mutually exclusive, so the embedded label is a fallback for orphaned records rather than an author name.
validation_method: cross-tabulation of null patterns

query: SELECT c.Id, c.PostId, c.UserId, c.UserDisplayName FROM comments c WHERE c.Text LIKE '%thank you user93%'; then the same rows joined to users on c.UserId
result: One matching comment, Id 53 on PostId 80, with a populated account reference and a null embedded label; resolving the account reference yields the name 'Preets'. Reading the embedded label instead would have returned nothing.
validation_method: text search followed by identity resolution against the user records

query: SELECT (OwnerUserId IS NULL), (OwnerDisplayName IS NULL), COUNT(*) FROM posts GROUP BY 1,2; plus a left join of posts to users on OwnerUserId
result: 89453 rows carry only the account reference; 1388 carry only the fallback label; 1121 carry both; 4 carry neither. Every non-null account reference resolves to a user row, and the fallback-label values are placeholder handles such as 'user28'.
validation_method: null cross-tabulation plus referential integrity check

query: SELECT DisplayName, COUNT(*) c FROM users GROUP BY 1 HAVING c>1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5
result: Repeated names are common: 'Chris' 80 accounts, 'John' 64, 'Alex' 63, 'Tom' 57, 'Michael' 52.
validation_method: duplicate value count

query: SELECT Id, DisplayName, Age, UpVotes FROM users WHERE DisplayName IN ('Tiago Pasqualini','Mark Meckes','Harvey Motulsky')
result: All three names resolve to exactly one account each: Id 16160 (Tiago Pasqualini, age 24, 0 up votes), Id 89 (Mark Meckes, age null, 61 up votes), Id 25 (Harvey Motulsky, age 62, 328 up votes). Distinctive full names are unambiguous even though common short names are not.
validation_method: name lookup resolving to account identifiers

query: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(Age), COUNT(DisplayName), COUNT(LastAccessDate), COUNT(CreationDate) FROM users
result: 40325 accounts total, but only 8318 have a recorded age, about 20.6 percent. Display name, last access and creation date are populated for every account.
validation_method: non-null count per column

query: SELECT MIN(Age), MAX(Age), AVG(Age) FROM users WHERE Age IS NOT NULL
result: Minimum 13, maximum 94, mean approximately 31.64 over the 8318 accounts that record an age.
validation_method: distribution summary over the populated subset

query: SELECT COUNT(UpVotes), COUNT(DownVotes) FROM users
result: UpVotes and DownVotes are populated for all 40325 accounts as lifetime counters on the profile, independent of the 38930 rows in the votes table.
validation_method: non-null count and semantic comparison against the vote table

query: SELECT VoteTypeId, COUNT(*) FROM votes GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
result: 1=1451, 2=33323, 3=444, 5=3365, 8=60, 9=59, 10=1, 11=44, 15=72, 16=111. Codes are numeric with no lookup table in the dataset; code 2 dominates and corresponds to up votes, code 3 to down votes.
validation_method: enumeration distribution

query: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(UserId), COUNT(PostId), COUNT(BountyAmount) FROM votes
result: 38930 vote rows total; only 3425 identify a voter, about 8.8 percent; PostId is populated for every row; BountyAmount for 101.
validation_method: non-null count per column

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts WHERE OwnerUserId=24; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM votes WHERE UserId=24
result: User 24 owns 10 posts and is recorded as the voter on 1 vote, giving a posts-to-votes ratio of 10.0.
validation_method: paired counts scoped to the same user identity

query: SELECT Name, COUNT(*) c FROM badges GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20
result: Badge names include 'Student' 14847, 'Supporter' 8828, 'Editor' 8453, 'Scholar' 6523, 'Teacher' 4679, plus many question- and answer-quality badges.
validation_method: enumeration distribution over the name column

query: SELECT substr(Date,1,4) y, COUNT(*) FROM badges WHERE Name='Student' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
validation_method: year bucketing of the award date for a single badge kind

query: SELECT LinkTypeId, COUNT(*) FROM postLinks GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
result: LinkTypeId 1=10186 and 3=916, numeric codes with no lookup table present in the dataset.
validation_method: enumeration distribution

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM postLinks pl LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.Id=pl.PostId LEFT JOIN posts r ON r.Id=pl.RelatedPostId WHERE p.Id IS NULL OR r.Id IS NULL
result: Only 4 of 11102 link records fail to resolve to a post row, so the endpoints are almost fully intact.
validation_method: referential integrity check

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE Id=-1; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts WHERE OwnerUserId=-1; SELECT Id, DisplayName FROM users WHERE Id=-1
result: Exactly one such account exists, named 'Community', and it is recorded as the owner of 211 posts. It is a system placeholder rather than a person.
validation_method: pseudo-account identification and usage count

query: PRAGMA table_info(posts); PRAGMA table_info(comments); plus sample values from each Score column
result: Both tables expose a column named Score, measuring votes on the respective entity. Comment scores include the value 17 and zero; post scores form a separate distribution on the post rows.
validation_method: side-by-side column identification in two tables

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE strftime('%Y',CreationDate)='2011'; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE LastAccessDate > '2014-09-01'
result: 4430 accounts were created in 2011; 5146 accounts last accessed the site after 2014-09-01. Both filters execute successfully against the text timestamps as stored.
validation_method: filtered count verification

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE LastAccessDate > '2014-09-01'
result: 5146 user accounts have a last-access timestamp later than 2014-09-01, out of 40325 accounts. The comparison executes directly against the text timestamps as stored.
validation_method: filtered count verification against the stored text timestamps
